testName: Kyiv, Podil -> Teremky: embankment and southern corridors instead of Povitryanykh Syl
description: The main route goes west over Peremohy/Povitryanykh Syl; both alternatives leave Podil along the Dnipro embankment. Used to be dropped: four shortcuts in a row cost more in detail than the hub graph said

testName: Kyiv, Podil -> Darnytskyi masyv: no main route with a loop bolted on
description: Used to return an alternative covering 99% of the main route plus a 3.3 km loop at the end

testName: Kyiv, Podil -> Berezniaky: centre offered, loop variant rejected
description: The alternative goes through the centre (Khreshchatyk, Parkova doroha) instead of the embankment; the candidate that only adds a loop avoids 0.3 km of the main route and must stay out

testName: Amstelveen, Fluweelboomlaan -> Westwijk: a 4 km route the hub graph cannot describe
description: The route never reaches the hub graph (two last-mile segments, no hub edge), so the alternatives can only come from the detailed road graph. Google offers three ways here; used to return none

testName: Tours -> Nouatre: the A10 corridor, where the second road is +33%
description: 83% of the fastest route is toll motorway (A10). Within +30% there is only one candidate, the main route with a 24 km loop bolted on (it avoids 3.2 km of it), so the list came back empty; the two real corridors are at +32.7% and +39.4% of cost

testName: Pisa -> Prato: a toll-free option next to 88% of toll motorway
description: The fastest route is A12 + A11. The alternatives are offered inside the normal limit here - one at +12% and one at +27% with only 9.7 km of toll left - which is what the fallback tier must not change

testName: Kyiv, a 1.7 km hop where the only other way costs 50% more
description: The route uses three hub segments, but only six hub points are settled by both trees and none of them carries a plateau, so the hub method returns nothing. The one distinct way round (2.5 km, +49.6%) is out of reach of a purely relative stretch limit

testName: Kyiv, a 2.5 km hop: both ways round offer less than a kilometre of their own
description: Two distinct ways round a 2.5 km route, at +13% and +25%. Each offers 0.9-1.2 km of roads the main route does not use, which is above ALT_MIN_DISTINCT_FLOOR (300 m) and far below the 1500 m the constant demanded before #25815: with the old value this route returns nothing.

testName: Kyiv, a 2.9 km hop that only the detailed graph can answer
description: Two alternatives at +38% and +45%, both out of reach of the relative stretch limit alone (ALT_STRETCH_ABS carries them) and both found only because the search falls back to the detailed graph when the hub graph returns nothing (#25872). Switching either off leaves the route with no alternatives at all, and so does ALT_MIN_DISTINCT_FLOOR = 1500.

testName: Amstelveen -> Amsterdam Zuidoost: no U-turn through both carriageways of Beneluxbaan
description: The reported case. A candidate used to drive 1.2 km down Beneluxbaan, turn round at Bovenkerkerweg and come back 2.6 km, returning within 56 m of where it left - the two hub points are the two carriageways of the same junction, 25 m apart, which neither the hub-index check nor the road-piece check can see. The best way between the two ends of that loop is 0.1 km.

testName: Kyiv west -> south-east: the cheapest corridor is offered, not its 145 s twin
description: Master offered an 18.2 km route with an 8.2 km loop where 1.5 km is enough. Once the candidates are built as two optimal legs the corridor comes out at 10.2 km, but only if the hub-graph sharing filter lets the candidate through: at ALT_MAX_SHARING = 0.6 the same corridor is offered 0.8 km longer and 145 s dearer.

unexpectedVia.name: the southern loop of the old candidate

testName: Badhoevedorp -> Almere: a 4 km loop where 72 m of road connects the two ends
description: The worst loop measured: the candidate came back to within 60 m of itself after 4.1 km, while the two ends are 72 m apart by road. With the candidates routed through their via node this route offers two corridors around Amsterdam instead.

unexpectedVia.name: the loop of the old candidate

testName: Amsterdam north -> east: a 2.1 km detour where 730 m is enough
description: A short route whose candidate went 2.1 km out and back while 730 m of road connects the two ends of that loop; the hub chain says nothing here, the detour is inside the expanded geometry. Guarded by the general loop check rather than by a point, because the corridor the faulty candidate looped through is also used by a sound alternative.

testName: Kyiv, Rusanivka -> Osokorky: the candidate that drives its own road twice
description: The one route of 105 measured where ALT_MAX_RETRACED still binds: without it a candidate is offered that covers a stretch of its own roads in both directions.

testName: Kyiv, Zhuliany -> Kharkivskyi: two cheap ways across the city
description: The city offers two ways east that cost under +7%, and both must be the ones proposed. Ranked on difference alone the second slot goes to a 35 km sweep around the city (+37%) instead, so this route measures ALT_STRETCH_PREFERRED: candidates within it are offered before the merely acceptable ones.

testName: Amsterdam, Sloten -> Slotermeer: the via node that has to be moved
description: Routing this candidate through its own via node still drives out and back, and only moving the via node past that detour produces the +8% way through the district. Without the move the candidate is dropped and its slot goes to a 3.6 km loop costing +58%.
